newsitem.title: USA: Titan Wheel files for notes, stock buyback.
newsitem.headline: Titan Wheel files for notes, stock buyback.

text.p: Titan Wheel International Inc filed a registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell up to $150 million in senior subordinated notes due 2007.

On February 25, the company will also begin an offer to purchase up to five million shares of its common stock at a price not greater than $15 nor less than $12.50 per share, for a maximum aggregate purchase price of $75 million.
The offer to purchase will expire on March 24 unless extended.
The repurchase is expected to be funded by the company partially from cash on hand and partially from increased borrowings under the credit bank facility, the filing said.
The offering is being made through Merrill Lynch & Co, Smith Barney Inc, Schroeder Wertheim & Co, Dean Witter Reynolds Inc and A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc.
Net proceeds will be used to repay outstanding long-term debt and, if the offer to purchase is not consummated, for general corporate purposes.
Titan, based in Quincy, Ill., is a global manufacturer of steel wheels and tires for off-highway vehicles used in the agricultural, consumer products, earthmoving/construction and military markets.
